Derive QC-relative thresholds from tagged quality-control samples

Source: R/quality-score.R
calibrate_thresholds_from_qc.Rd

Replaces the absolute green/amber thresholds of a scoring table with values anchored on the experiment's own QC sample(s): green is set to the QC median of each metric and amber to that median relaxed by slack (downward for higher_better metrics, upward for lower_better). This is what lets the score be calibrated without any external benchmark dataset. Metrics whose QC median is NA keep their default thresholds.

Usage

calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(
  metrics,
  qc_samples,
  thresholds = quality_thresholds_default(),
  slack = 0.2
)

Arguments

metrics

Output of qc_metrics_by_sample().

qc_samples

Character vector of Sample values flagged as QC controls.

thresholds

A scoring table to recalibrate (default quality_thresholds_default()); its direction/weight/label are kept.

slack

Fractional tolerance for the amber band (default 0.2, i.e. amber = green × 0.8 for higher-better, green × 1.2 for lower-better).

Value

The thresholds table with green/amber recomputed from the QC samples where possible.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
m <- qc_metrics_by_sample(pep_all, c(8, 13), "MHC1")
calibrate_thresholds_from_qc(m, qc_samples = c("QC_A", "QC_B"))
} # }
